Definition: from G3846; a similitude ("parable"), i.e. (symbolic) fictitious narrative (of common life conveying a moral), apothegm or adage:--comparison, figure, parable, proverb.
BiblicalUsage: Parabolē is the parable, the similitude laid beside a truth so it can be seen. Jesus speaks many things unto them in parables, and without a parable He speaks not unto them; He teaches the multitude in parables, and He speaks the parable of the lost sheep to the murmuring Pharisees.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the parable is Jesus' chosen way of teaching. A story laid beside the truth, so that those with ears to hear find it and those without pass it by.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
